texts.facts: These petitions have filed us/ 166 of M.V Act seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a RTA. As both the petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 14.01.2024 at about 5.10 p.m., the petitioner in MVC No.775/2024 (as a rider) and petitioner in MVC No.774/2024 (as a pillion rider) were proceeding on a Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KF-2907 slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations. When they reached Opposite to AMC College, Kalkere, Jigani Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-37-CQ-6073 was going ahead of the petitioners motorcycle in the same direction, with high speed in rash and negligent manner without showing any signal all of a sudden applied brake and stopped and then to swered his vehicle towards left side of the road as a result the rider / petitioner in MVC.775/2024 could not control his vehicle and dashed to the hind portion of the Lorry. Due to the said impact, both the rider and pillion rider Sagar R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73211830/ 2 fell down and sustained grievous injuries. 3. It is further urged that immediately after the accident petitioners in both the petitions were shifted to Sankalpa Multispeciality Hospital wherein they treatment and discharged 4 SCCH-23 MVC.774/2024 C/w MVC.775/2024 with an advised to take follow-up treatment. They have spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses. On account of the accidental injuries the petitioners have suffered permanent disablement. Further it is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent act of the driver of Lorry. The respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount. Hence prayed to allow the petitions. 4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 did not appear before this Tribunal. Hence he placed exparte. 5. After service of notice, respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement in both the petitions and contending that the petitions itself are not maintainable either law or on facts. The petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties. The respondent No.1 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-37-CQ-6073. However the liability if 5 SCCH-23 Sagar R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73211830/ 3 MVC.774/2024 C/w MVC.775/2024 any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy. Non -compliance of sections 158(6), 170 of MV Act is pleaded. This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident. Further negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle is denied. Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident. Further the rider of the motorcycle also not possess valid DL as on the date of accident. On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him. Further denied all the allegation made in the petitions. Hence prayed to dismiss the petitions. The petitioner in MVC.774/2024 examined himself as PW.1. Ex's .P1 to 10 and Ex.P.14 to 16 were marked on his behalf. The petitioner in MVC.775/2024 examined himself as PW.2. Ex's .P11 to 13 and Ex.P.17 to 19 were marked on his behalf. The petitioners have examined the MRO and Billing Manager of Sankalpa Mulstispeciality Hospital as PW.3 and through him Ex.P.20 to 26 were got marked. The petitioner in MVC.774/2024 was examined Dr. Nagaraj. B.N as PW.4 and through him got marked Ex.P.27 & 28 documents. In order to 7 SCCH-23 MVC.774/2024 C/w MVC.775/2024 prove the defence, the respondent No.1 got examined its official as RW.1 and through him got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents. This tribunal answers to the above issues in both the petitions are as follows :- MVC.774/2024 & MVC.775/2024 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following : REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 IN BOTH PETITIONS : The petitioners filed their affidavits reiterating the averments of the petitions. To corroborate their oral testimony they have produced police documents viz., Ex.P1 to 8 and Ex.P.11. The evidence of PW's.1 Sagar R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73211830/ 5 & 2 is fortified by the above documents, which go to show that based on the Complaint the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the Lorry for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 8 SCCH-23 MVC.774/2024 C/w MVC.775/2024 337, 338 of IPC.
texts.arguments: Further respondent No.1 taken up the contention that the rider of motorcycle was under intoxication of alcohol and that has contributed for the accident. He stated that as per police intimation letters dated.14.01.2024 i.e., Ex.P.25 and 26 both of the petitioners had consumed alcohol at the time of accident, it clearly shows that the accident occurred due to the negligence of rider of motorcycle as per hospital records while they themselves fell down and sustained injuries and there was no involvement of the lorry in the accident. During the course of cross examination RW.1 stated that he has not seen the accident and further the police have filed charge sheet against their insured 9 SCCH-23 MVC.774/2024 C/w MVC.775/2024 vehicle. He admitted that no documents were produced to show Sagar R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73211830/ 6 that the rider was driving under the influence of alcohol. 11. In this regard the respondent No.1 relied on the decision reported in ILR 2012 KAR 2689, in the case of K.E.Basavarajappa V/s H. Chandrappa and another and further relied on the judgment of Honble High Court in MFA.2300/2016(MV-D) in the case of Smt. Rathnamma and others V/s HDFC Ergo Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd. It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023. Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under : "(b) The accident is of the year 2017. The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum. 13 SCCH-23 Sagar R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73211830/ 9 MVC.774/2024 C/w MVC.775/2024 income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant" Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
